NTT and Telwel plan sensor-based cleaning quality service

Targeting April 2027, the service would use cleanliness and building-use data to support outcome-based contracts.

NTT DOCOMO BUSINESS ↗26 October 2026English editorial summary
StoryImages 3

Measuring cleaning outcomes

Telwel West Japan and NTT DOCOMO BUSINESS have begun developing a cleaning quality-assurance service targeting April 2027. Shared measures would let customers and providers define service-level agreements around cleanliness outcomes rather than only staffing and cleaning frequency.

Combining several measurements

The plan combines ATP, odor, color-difference and gloss measurements with restroom-use and bin-fill sensors. Image-based dirt recognition is also under development and consideration. A dashboard would flag locations below SLA targets and provide evidence for reports and improvement decisions.

People and robots have complementary roles

Telwel will design evaluation, SLA terms and operating processes; NTT will connect sensors and develop analytics, AI and robot-assisted management. The partners intend to combine human and robotic cleaning and later extend to building operations. Quantified savings and general service availability are not yet demonstrated.
